stem:
From the concentrations of \(\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Cl}\) (butyl chloride) at different times given below, calculate the average rate of the reaction:

\(\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Cl} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{OH} + \text{HCl}\)

during different intervals of time.

| \(t/\text{s}\) | 0 | 50 | 100 | 150 | 200 | 300 | 400 | 700 | 800 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| \([\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Cl}]/\text{mol L}^{-1}\) | 0.100 | 0.0905 | 0.0820 | 0.0741 | 0.0671 | 0.0549 | 0.0439 | 0.0210 | 0.017 |
solution:
We can determine the difference in concentration over different intervals of time and thus determine the average rate by dividing \(\Delta[\text{R}]\) by \(\Delta t\) (Table 3.1).

**Table 3.1: Average rates of hydrolysis of butyl chloride**

| \([\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Cl}]_{t_1}/\text{mol L}^{-1}\) | \([\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Cl}]_{t_2}/\text{mol L}^{-1}\) | \(t_1/\text{s}\) | \(t_2/\text{s}\) | \(r_{av} \times 10^{4}/\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1} = -\left\{\left([\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Cl}]_{t_2} - [\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{Cl}]_{t_1}\right)/(t_2 - t_1)\right\} \times 10^{4}\) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.100 | 0.0905 | 0 | 50 | 1.90 |
| 0.0905 | 0.0820 | 50 | 100 | 1.70 |
| 0.0820 | 0.0741 | 100 | 150 | 1.58 |
| 0.0741 | 0.0671 | 150 | 200 | 1.40 |
| 0.0671 | 0.0549 | 200 | 300 | 1.22 |
| 0.0549 | 0.0439 | 300 | 400 | 1.10 |
| 0.0439 | 0.0335 | 400 | 500 | 1.04 |
| 0.0210 | 0.017 | 700 | 800 | 0.4 |
_note: Transcribed faithfully. The book's own Table 3.1 (the printed solution) contains a row \(0.0439 \rightarrow 0.0335\) over \(400\text{-}500\,\text{s}\), but the question's data table prints NO entry at \(t = 500\,\text{s}\) and never lists the concentration 0.0335 — so that row of the solution uses data the question does not supply. Every other row is reproducible from the stem's table, and the 1.04 value is itself consistent with 0.0439/0.0335 over 100 s. Also as printed: the final concentration is given to 3 dp (0.017) where every other entry carries 4 dp.

stem:
The decomposition of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\) in \(\text{CCl}_4\) at 318K has been studied by monitoring the concentration of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\) in the solution. Initially the concentration of \(\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\) is \(2.33\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\) and after 184 minutes, it is reduced to \(2.08\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\). The reaction takes place according to the equation

\(2\,\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\,(g) \rightarrow 4\,\text{NO}_2\,(g) + \text{O}_2\,(g)\)

Calculate the average rate of this reaction in terms of hours, minutes and seconds. What is the rate of production of \(\text{NO}_2\) during this period?
solution:
Average Rate \(= \dfrac{1}{2}\left\{-\dfrac{\Delta[\text{N}_2\text{O}_5]}{\Delta t}\right\} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\left[\dfrac{(2.08 - 2.33)\,\text{mol L}^{-1}}{184\,\text{min}}\right]\)

\(= 6.79 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{mol L}^{-1}/\text{min} = (6.79 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{min}^{-1}) \times (60\,\text{min}/1\text{h})\)

\(= 4.07 \times 10^{-2}\,\text{mol L}^{-1}/\text{h}\)

\(= 6.79 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{mol L}^{-1} \times 1\,\text{min}/60\,\text{s}\)

\(= 1.13 \times 10^{-5}\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\)

It may be remembered that

Rate \(= \dfrac{1}{4}\left\{\dfrac{\Delta[\text{NO}_2]}{\Delta t}\right\}\)

\(\dfrac{\Delta[\text{NO}_2]}{\Delta t} = 6.79 \times 10^{-4} \times 4\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{min}^{-1} = 2.72 \times 10^{-3}\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{min}^{-1}\)
_note: Transcribed as printed. In the fourth line of the printed solution the book writes \(6.79 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{mol L}^{-1} \times 1\,\text{min}/60\,\text{s}\), dropping the \(\text{min}^{-1}\) that the same quantity carries two lines above; the numerical result \(1.13 \times 10^{-5}\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\) is nevertheless correct. Also as printed: the stem describes decomposition in \(\text{CCl}_4\) solution while the equation labels every species (g).

stem: For the reaction \(\text{R} \rightarrow \text{P}\), the concentration of a reactant changes from 0.03M to 0.02M in 25 minutes. Calculate the average rate of reaction using units of time both in minutes and seconds.

In a reaction, \(2\text{A} \rightarrow\) Products, the concentration of A decreases from \(0.5\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\) to \(0.4\,\text{mol L}^{-1}\) in 10 minutes. Calculate the rate during this interval?

subtopic: Factors Influencing Rate of a Reaction
stem:
Calculate the overall order of a reaction which has the rate expression

(a) Rate \(= k\,[\text{A}]^{1/2}\,[\text{B}]^{3/2}\)

(b) Rate \(= k\,[\text{A}]^{3/2}\,[\text{B}]^{-1}\)
solution:
(a) Rate \(= k\,[\text{A}]^{x}\,[\text{B}]^{y}\)

order \(= x + y\)

So order \(= 1/2 + 3/2 = 2\), i.e., second order

(b) order \(= 3/2 + (-1) = 1/2\), i.e., half order.

subtopic: Factors Influencing Rate of a Reaction
stem:
Identify the reaction order from each of the following rate constants.

(i) \(k = 2.3 \times 10^{-5}\,\text{L mol}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\)

(ii) \(k = 3 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{s}^{-1}\)
solution:
(i) The unit of second order rate constant is \(\text{L mol}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\), therefore \(k = 2.3 \times 10^{-5}\,\text{L mol}^{-1}\text{s}^{-1}\) represents a second order reaction.

(ii) The unit of a first order rate constant is \(\text{s}^{-1}\) therefore \(k = 3 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{s}^{-1}\) represents a first order reaction.
